conditions.title: Scapula anterior tilt
conditions.summary: Anterior tipping of the scapula can reduce comfortable overhead mechanics and contribute to shoulder compensation.

conditions.title: Round shoulder
conditions.tags: Upper crossed syndrome, shoulder impingement, rib flare
conditions.tightMuscles: Pectoralis minor, pectoralis major, latissimus dorsi
conditions.summary: A forward shoulder position commonly combines restricted anterior tissue with reduced scapular control.

conditions.title: Ankle sprain recovery
conditions.tags: Balance, mobility, stability, return to movement
conditions.tightMuscles: Varies by injury stage and individual presentation
conditions.weakMuscles: Calf and lateral ankle strength may require progressive rebuilding
conditions.screening: Comfortable walking, swelling response, ankle range, balance, and task tolerance
conditions.summary: Ankle recovery is a progressive process of restoring comfortable motion, balance, strength, and confidence after the acute stage has settled.

muscles.title: Serratus anterior
muscles.origin: Upper eight or nine ribs
muscles.insertion: Anterior medial border of the scapula
muscles.actions: Protracts the scapula, assists upward rotation, and helps hold the scapula against the rib cage.
muscles.imageAlt: Anatomical illustration highlighting the serratus anterior muscle on the side of the rib cage
muscles.imageCredit: Serratus anterior, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Lower trapezius
muscles.origin: Lower thoracic spinous processes
muscles.insertion: Medial end of the scapular spine
muscles.actions: The lower fibers assist scapular depression and upward rotation and contribute to posterior tilt during arm elevation.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical illustration highlighting the trapezius muscle
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Pectoralis minor
muscles.origin: Ribs three to five
muscles.insertion: Coracoid process of the scapula
muscles.actions: Draws the scapula anteriorly and inferiorly against the thoracic wall and may assist forced inspiration when the scapula is fixed.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the pectoralis minor muscle
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Sternocleidomastoid
muscles.origin: Manubrium of the sternum and medial clavicle
muscles.insertion: Mastoid process of the temporal bone and lateral superior nuchal line
muscles.actions: Bilaterally flexes the neck; unilaterally laterally flexes to the same side and rotates the head to the opposite side.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Deltoid
muscles.origin: Lateral clavicle, acromion, and spine of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of the humerus
muscles.actions: Primarily abducts the arm; anterior fibers assist flexion and medial rotation, while posterior fibers assist extension and lateral rotation.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Pectoralis major
muscles.origin: Medial clavicle, sternum, and costal cartilages of the upper ribs
muscles.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus
muscles.actions: Adducts and medially rotates the arm; the clavicular fibers assist shoulder flexion.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Latissimus dorsi
muscles.origin: Lower thoracic vertebrae, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, and lower ribs
muscles.insertion: Floor of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus
muscles.actions: Extends, adducts, and medially rotates the arm.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Biceps brachii
muscles.origin: Coracoid process and supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Radial tuberosity and forearm fascia through the bicipital aponeurosis
muscles.actions: Flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm; also assists shoulder flexion.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Triceps brachii
muscles.origin: Infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula and posterior humerus
muscles.insertion: Olecranon of the ulna
muscles.actions: Extends the elbow; the long head also assists shoulder extension and adduction.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Brachioradialis
muscles.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Lateral distal radius near the styloid process
muscles.actions: Flexes the elbow most effectively with the forearm in a neutral position.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Rectus abdominis
muscles.origin: Pubic crest and pubic symphysis
muscles.insertion: Xiphoid process and costal cartilages of ribs five through seven
muscles.actions: Flexes the trunk, compresses abdominal contents, and assists control of pelvic position.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: External oblique
muscles.origin: External surfaces of ribs five through twelve
muscles.insertion: Linea alba, pubic tubercle, and anterior iliac crest
muscles.actions: Compresses the abdomen; flexes and laterally flexes the trunk; rotates the trunk to the opposite side.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Transversus abdominis
muscles.origin: Thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, inguinal ligament, and internal surfaces of lower costal cartilages
muscles.insertion: Linea alba and pubis
muscles.actions: Compresses and supports abdominal contents and contributes to trunk stabilization and forced expiration.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Erector spinae
muscles.origin: Broad tendon from the posterior iliac crest, sacrum, and lumbar spinous processes
muscles.insertion: Ribs and transverse or spinous processes extending toward the cervical region and skull
muscles.actions: Bilaterally extends the vertebral column; unilaterally assists lateral flexion and postural control.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Diaphragm
muscles.origin: Xiphoid process, lower ribs and costal cartilages, and upper lumbar vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Central tendon of the diaphragm
muscles.actions: Primary muscle of inspiration; contraction increases thoracic volume and supports pressure management through the trunk.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Gluteus maximus
muscles.origin: Posterior ilium, sacrum, coccyx, and sacrotuberous ligament
muscles.insertion: Iliotibial tract and gluteal tuberosity of the femur
muscles.actions: Extends and laterally rotates the hip and contributes to powerful rising, climbing, and propulsion.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Gluteus medius
muscles.origin: External surface of the ilium between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines
muscles.insertion: Lateral surface of the greater trochanter of the femur
muscles.actions: Abducts the hip and helps stabilize the pelvis during single-leg support; anterior fibers assist medial rotation.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Iliopsoas
muscles.origin: Lumbar vertebrae and iliac fossa
muscles.insertion: Lesser trochanter of the femur
muscles.actions: Powerfully flexes the hip and can assist trunk flexion or postural control depending on which attachment is fixed.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Adductor longus
muscles.origin: Body of the pubis inferior to the pubic crest
muscles.insertion: Middle third of the linea aspera of the femur
muscles.actions: Adducts the hip and assists hip flexion and medial rotation.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Rectus femoris
muscles.origin: Anterior inferior iliac spine and ilium superior to the acetabulum
muscles.insertion: Tibial tuberosity through the quadriceps tendon, patella, and patellar ligament
muscles.actions: Extends the knee and flexes the hip.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Biceps femoris
muscles.origin: Ischial tuberosity and linea aspera of the femur
muscles.insertion: Head of the fibula
muscles.actions: Flexes the knee and laterally rotates the flexed leg; the long head also extends the hip.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Tibialis anterior
muscles.origin: Lateral condyle and upper lateral surface of the tibia
muscles.insertion: Medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal
muscles.actions: Dorsiflexes and inverts the foot and helps control the foot as it lowers during walking.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Gastrocnemius
muscles.origin: Posterior surfaces of the medial and lateral femoral condyles
muscles.insertion: Posterior calcaneus through the calcaneal tendon
muscles.actions: Plantarflexes the ankle and assists knee flexion; contributes strongly to propulsion.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Soleus
muscles.origin: Posterior fibular head and proximal fibula, and soleal line of the tibia
muscles.insertion: Posterior calcaneus through the calcaneal tendon
muscles.actions: Plantarflexes the ankle and plays an important postural role during standing and walking.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Fibularis longus
muscles.origin: Head and upper lateral surface of the fibula
muscles.insertion: Base of the first metatarsal and medial cuneiform on the plantar foot
muscles.actions: Everts and plantarflexes the foot and helps support the transverse and lateral arches.
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

recipes.title: Squat preparation
recipes.goal: Improve comfortable squat depth and reassess symptoms
recipes.equipment: Vibrating massage ball, open floor space
recipes.steps:
1. Release the hamstrings with a vibrating massage ball.
2. Perform a controlled splitting stretch.
3. Execute a full squat and reassess pain and movement quality.
recipes.cautions: Stop if pain increases or symptoms radiate. This is education, not diagnosis.

recipes.title: Scapular control sequence
recipes.goal: Restore comfortable scapular movement before loaded overhead work
recipes.steps:
1. Address rib flare and breathing position.
2. Use gentle pectoralis minor mobility if indicated.
3. Practice serratus anterior control.
4. Reassess overhead reach.
recipes.cautions: Use a pain-free range and avoid forcing the shoulder into end range.

recipes.title: Ankle rehabilitation progression
recipes.goal: Rebuild comfortable ankle motion, balance, strength, and confidence after an ankle sprain
recipes.steps:
1. Begin only after the acute stage has settled and exercise has been cleared.
2. Restore comfortable ankle motion without forcing symptoms.
3. Rebuild balance and controlled weight bearing.
4. Progress calf and ankle strength gradually.
5. Reassess walking and task tolerance before advancing.
recipes.cautions: Stop and seek clinical guidance if pain or swelling increases, the ankle gives way, or walking remains difficult.
